name: Neo-Confucianism
summary: Neo-Confucianism is the Song-Ming revival of Confucian thought, systematised by Zhu Xi from the Northern Song masters and the Four Books, which grounds ethics in a cosmic principle (li) and makes self-cultivation the root of order. Its politics are moral: the state is ordered by the ruler's own virtue and example, beginning with the regulated family, and gain is not the state's prosperity. It opposes selfishness (si) in favour of public spirit (gong) and sought to restore China's Confucian culture; Zhu Xi even proposed a committee of moral experts to check imperial decisions.
scope: The Cheng-Zhu school (Cheng Yi, Cheng Hao, Zhu Xi) as the state-orthodox Neo-Confucianism (daoxue, lixue) of the Song through Qing dynasties, as the IEP and SEP present it: Zhu Xi's synthesis of Zhou Dunyi, Zhang Zai and the Cheng brothers, built on the Four Books (Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, Doctrine of the Mean) and the anthology Reflections on Things at Hand. Wang Yangming's mind-school (xinxue) is used only where it does not diverge from it. It is a moral philosophy with political implications, not a modern political programme; Korean, Japanese and Vietnamese variants and modern New Confucianism are not the basis.
